newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia probing commodity board irregularities.
newsitem.headline: Croatia probing commodity board irregularities.

text.p: The Croatian parliament on Friday set up a commission to investigate allegations of malpractices in the work of the state commodities reserve board relating to wheat and corn exports, the state news agency HINA said.

The state auditing commission recently found evidence of fraud in transactions of the state reserve board, Drzavno Ravnateljstvo za Robne Rezerve, and various entrepreneurs it had contracted for wheat exports, HINA said.
In one case, auditors said an entrepreneur purchased wheat from the board at a reduced price and later exported it at a higher price, costing the board 19 million kuna ($3.4 million).

The board came under scrutiny earlier this year when bread prices rose amid speculation that some of the 80,000 tonnes of wheat from reserves intended for the Croatian market had been exported illegally after the world price went up.
Fearing shortages, the government imported 10,000 tonnes of wheat flour and banned all exports of wheat until next year's crop.
The "wheat affair" revealed disorder in Croatian storages which apart from state commmodities contain goods like clothing, footwear and even vehicles.
Those were amassed under the former Yugoslav federal government, but the exact quantity of reserves had been always kept secret.

HINA said parliament decided on Friday to make the reserves board a part of the Economy Ministry to improve its accountability. Previously, it was a semi-autonomous entity reporting only to parliament.
HINA said the parliamentary commission would determine all relevant facts about the wheat and corn exports and wheat flour imports to establish whether Croatian economic interests were damaged.
The probe was to be completed within six months.
